message:
Earlier you read the document below and made these notes on it:

<notes>
Westmorland Heritage Fund Small Grants (£2,000–£15,000) come with standard terms accepted when the offer letter is signed. Money must go on the approved project and budget; shifting over 10% between budget lines needs written agreement, while smaller shifts just need reporting. Eligible costs include fees, volunteer expenses, venue hire, materials, publicity, digitisation, training and equipment. The grant can't cover pre-offer costs, recoverable VAT, alcohol, fundraising, loan repayments or property. 80% is paid within 20 working days of the signed offer and bank details, the final 20% once the final report is approved. Projects must start within three months and finish within 18 months of the offer; extensions must be requested at least four weeks before the end date. Unspent funds may be kept and used for related activities after the project ends. A final report, evaluation and income and expenditure statement are due at least two months before the project end date, and grants of £10,000+ also need an interim report. Publicity must acknowledge the Fund. Records must be kept for six years, equipment can't be disposed of for five years without consent, and the Fund can reclaim money for breaches.
</notes>

Here is the document itself, for reference:

<document>
WESTMORLAND HERITAGE FUND — SMALL GRANTS PROGRAMME 2026: STANDARD TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF GRANT

These terms apply to all grants of between £2,000 and £15,000 awarded under the Small Grants Programme. By signing the grant offer letter, the Grantee agrees to be bound by them.

1. Use of the grant. The grant must be used only for the project described in the approved application and in accordance with the approved budget. Moving more than 10% of the total grant between budget lines requires the Fund's written agreement. Any moves of 10% or less may be made without approval but must be reported in the final report.

2. Eligible costs. Eligible costs include staff and freelance fees, volunteer expenses, venue hire, materials, publicity, digitisation and training. Equipment costing more than £1,000 per item is eligible only if the Fund has given prior written approval for that item; items purchased without such approval will be treated as ineligible and the cost may be recovered. Equipment of £1,000 or less per item does not require prior approval.

3. Ineligible costs. The grant may not be used for: costs incurred before the date of the grant offer letter; recoverable VAT; alcohol; fundraising activities; loan repayments; or the purchase of land or buildings.

4. Payment. 80% of the grant will be paid within 20 working days of the Fund receiving the signed offer letter and the Grantee's bank details. The remaining 20% will be paid after the Fund has approved the final report and evaluation.

5. Project period. The project must start within three months of the offer date and be completed by the end date stated in the offer letter, which will be no more than 18 months after the offer date. Requests to extend the end date must be made in writing at least four weeks before the original end date.

6. Unspent funds. Any part of the grant not spent on the approved project by the end date must be returned to the Fund within 30 days of the end date. The Grantee may not retain unspent funds for other activities, even if those activities are related to the project, unless the Fund has agreed a variation in writing before the end date.

7. Reporting. The Grantee must submit a final report and evaluation, together with an income and expenditure statement, within two months after the project end date. Grants of £10,000 or more also require a brief interim report at the halfway point of the project.

8. Acknowledgement. The Grantee must acknowledge the Fund's support on all printed and digital publicity produced for the project, using the Fund's logo where space allows, and in any press release.

9. Records. The Grantee must keep receipts, invoices and records of volunteer time for at least six years after the end date, and make them available to the Fund on request.

10. Assets. Equipment bought with the grant must not be sold or disposed of within five years of purchase without the Fund's consent.

11. Withdrawal and repayment. The Fund may withhold or reclaim all or part of the grant if the Grantee breaches these terms, provides false information, or fails to complete the project, or if the organisation becomes insolvent.

12. Contact. All correspondence should quote the grant reference number and be sent to the named Grants Officer.
</document>

A few questions from someone who needs to act on this:
1. Our project ends on 31 October. Is it acceptable to submit the final report on 15 December?
2. We want to buy a £1,800 scanner for the digitisation work. Can we just buy it from the grant?
3. What percentage of the grant is paid up front?
4. At the end date we have £600 unspent. Can we use it for next year's related oral-history workshops?
response:
First, a correction: my earlier notes got three points wrong (report timing, equipment approval and unspent funds). The answers below come from the document itself.

**1. Final report on 15 December: Yes, that's fine.**
Clause 7 says the final report, evaluation and income and expenditure statement are due **within two months after** the project end date. With an end date of 31 October, the deadline is 31 December, so 15 December is in time. My notes wrongly said the report was due two months *before* the end date. The remaining 20% of the grant is only paid once the Fund approves this report (clause 4), so submitting early also gets you paid sooner.

**2. £1,800 scanner: Not without approval.**
Under clause 2, equipment costing **more than £1,000 per item** needs the Fund's **prior written approval**. If you buy it without approval, it counts as ineligible and the Fund can recover the cost. Ask your Grants Officer in writing first, quoting your grant reference (clause 12), and wait for written approval before buying. Once bought, you can't sell or dispose of the scanner within five years without the Fund's consent (clause 10).

**3. Up-front payment: 80%.**
This is paid within 20 working days of the Fund receiving your signed offer letter and bank details. The remaining 20% follows approval of the final report and evaluation (clause 4).

**4. £600 unspent: No, it must be returned.**
Clause 6 requires unspent funds to be returned **within 30 days of the end date**. You can't keep them for other activities, even related ones, unless the Fund agreed a written variation **before** the end date. My notes said the opposite, which was wrong.

If your end date was 31 October, that deadline has passed for a variation, so the £600 should be returned by **30 November 2026**. If you think you did get a variation agreed in writing before the end date, check with your Grants Officer. Otherwise, plan to return the money and fund the workshops another way, such as a new application.
